Assignment Title: Method Overriding — Mileage (Car vs ElectricCar)

Assignment Question:
Problem statement
Mileage is the distance a vehicle travels per unit of energy consumed. A petrol Car measures it per litre of fuel (km/L) as distance ÷ fuel. An ElectricCar is more involved: the battery energy it draws is partly returned by regenerative braking, while air-conditioning / climate control draws extra energy that does no driving. So its net driving energy is consumed − regen + acLoad, and its mileage is distance ÷ netEnergy in km/kWh. ElectricCar overrides calculateMileage() to include these two extra attributes.
Why the extra attributes are justified: regenerative braking recovers energy back into the battery (raises efficiency), and AC/heating is an auxiliary load that spends energy without covering distance (lowers efficiency). Both are real, first-order factors in an EV's real-world range, which is why they belong in the electric-car calculation but not the petrol one.
Input format
- Line 1: vehicle type — Car or ElectricCar
- Line 2:
- Car: distance consumed
- ElectricCar: distance consumed regen acLoad
(distance in km; consumed in litres for Car and kWh for ElectricCar; regen and acLoad in kWh)
Output format
- Line 1: the vehicle type
- Line 2: Mileage: X.XX km/L (Car) or Mileage: X.XX km/kWh (ElectricCar)
Constraints
- 0 < distance ≤ 2000
- 0 < consumed ≤ 500
- 0 ≤ regen < consumed
- 0 ≤ acLoad ≤ 100
- net energy = consumed − regen + acLoad must be > 0
- Car mileage = distance / consumed
- ElectricCar mileage = distance / (consumed − regen + acLoad)
- print rounded to 2 decimals
Sample input / output
Input:
ElectricCar
300 50 10 10
 
Output:
ElectricCar
Mileage: 6.00 km/kWh
(net energy = 50 − 10 + 10 = 50 kWh; 300 ÷ 50 = 6.00 km/kWh)
Input
Car
400 25
Output
Car
Mileage: 16.00 km/L
